_comment: MA3 Analysis Tab Feedback Messages - Instructors can edit these
NAME_PRESENT: Your name in cell B10 is complete.
NAME_MISSING: Your name is missing from cell B10. Type your full name there so your work can be matched to you.
NAME_TOO_SHORT: The name in cell B10 ('{name}') looks too short. It needs your full first and last name.
DIFF_ALL_CORRECT_ARRAY: Your differences use the array formula {formula}, which is correct for all 50 rows.
DIFF_FORMULA_MISSING: Your difference in {cell} is missing. Enter =C{row}-B{row} (After minus Before).
DIFF_FORMULA_WRONG: Your difference in {cell} ({found}) is not After minus Before. Change it to =C{row}-B{row}.
DIFF_NOT_FORMULA: Your difference in {cell} is a typed value, not a formula. Use a formula that subtracts the Before score from the After score, like =C14-B14 in D14.
DIFF_ARRAY_WRONG: Your array formula in {cell} ({found}) does not give After minus Before. Change it to =C14:C63-B14:B63.
STAT_MEAN_WRONG: Your mean in {cell} is not right. Use AVERAGE on that column's 50 values: =AVERAGE(B14:B63) in G18, C14:C63 in H18, and D14:D63 in I18.
STAT_MEAN_MISSING: Your mean in {cell} is missing. Enter =AVERAGE( ) over that column's 50 values: B14:B63 for G18, C14:C63 for H18, D14:D63 for I18.
STAT_MEAN_PARTIAL: Your mean in {cell} is close but not quite right: {hint}.
STAT_MEDIAN_WRONG: Your median in {cell} is not right. Use MEDIAN on that column's 50 values: =MEDIAN(B14:B63) in G19, C14:C63 in H19, and D14:D63 in I19.
STAT_MEDIAN_MISSING: Your median in {cell} is missing. Enter =MEDIAN( ) over that column's 50 values: B14:B63 for G19, C14:C63 for H19, D14:D63 for I19.
STAT_MEDIAN_PARTIAL: Your median in {cell} is close but not quite right: {hint}.
STAT_STDEV_OK: Your standard deviation in {cell} is correct.
STAT_STDEV_WRONG: Your standard deviation in {cell} is not right. Use STDEV.S (or STDEV) on that column's 50 values: =STDEV.S(B14:B63) in G20, C14:C63 in H20, and D14:D63 in I20.
STAT_STDEV_MISSING: Your standard deviation in {cell} is missing. Enter =STDEV.S( ) over that column's 50 values: B14:B63 for G20, C14:C63 for H20, D14:D63 for I20.
STAT_STDEV_PARTIAL: Your standard deviation in {cell} is close but not quite right: {hint}.
STAT_RANGE_WRONG: Your range in {cell} is not right. It should be the largest value minus the smallest, e.g. =MAX(B14:B63)-MIN(B14:B63) in G21 (use C14:C63 in H21 and D14:D63 in I21).
STAT_RANGE_MISSING: Your range in {cell} is missing. Enter MAX minus MIN of that column, e.g. =MAX(B14:B63)-MIN(B14:B63) in G21 (C14:C63 in H21, D14:D63 in I21).
STAT_RANGE_PARTIAL: Your range in {cell} is close but not quite right: {hint}.
PERCENTILE_WRONG: Your percentile in {cell} needs a fix: {reason}. Use =PERCENTILE.INC(D14:D63, k), where k is the percentile shown in column F as a decimal (25th is 0.25).
PERCENTILE_MISSING: Your percentile in {cell} is missing. Enter =PERCENTILE.INC(D14:D63, k), where k is the percentile shown in column F as a decimal (25th is 0.25).
EMPIRICAL_LOWER_OK: Your lower bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is correct.
EMPIRICAL_LOWER_WRONG: Your lower bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is not right. It should be the mean minus the standard deviation of the differences: =I18-I20.
EMPIRICAL_LOWER_MISSING: Your lower bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is missing. Enter the mean minus the standard deviation of the differences: =I18-I20.
EMPIRICAL_LOWER_PARTIAL: Your lower bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is close but not quite right. {hint} Use =I18-I20.
EMPIRICAL_UPPER_OK: Your upper bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is correct.
EMPIRICAL_UPPER_WRONG: Your upper bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is not right. It should be the mean plus the standard deviation of the differences: =I18+I20.
EMPIRICAL_UPPER_MISSING: Your upper bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is missing. Enter the mean plus the standard deviation of the differences: =I18+I20.
EMPIRICAL_UPPER_PARTIAL: Your upper bound for the empirical rule ({cell}) is close but not quite right. {hint} Use =I18+I20.
WRITTEN_MISSING: The written analysis for section 5b is missing. Please write your interpretation of the results.
WRITTEN_TOO_SHORT: Your written analysis looks brief ({length} characters). Make sure it fully answers the question.
FORMAT_CELL_WRONG: Your {cell} is not showing 2 decimal places. Set it to Number with 2 decimal places (Home > Number Format).
